title: Judges Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 7.

questions.question: Where did Gideon and his people pitch their camp?
options: Beside the well of Harod
Near the Jordan River
On Mount Gilead
By the hill of Moreh
questions.correctAnswer: Beside the well of Harod
questions.explanation: Judges 7:1 states that Gideon and all the people pitched beside the well of Harod.

questions.question: Why did the LORD say the people with Gideon were too many?
options: So Israel would not boast that they saved themselves
Because they were not well armed
Because they would get lost in the valley
Because they were tired and weak
questions.correctAnswer: So Israel would not boast that they saved themselves
questions.explanation: Judges 7:2 explains that the people were too many so that Israel would not say, 'Mine own hand hath saved me.'

questions.question: How many men returned home when those who were fearful and afraid were told to depart?
options: Twenty-two thousand
Ten thousand
Three hundred
Five thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-two thousand
questions.explanation: Judges 7:3 states that twenty-two thousand returned, leaving ten thousand remaining.

questions.question: What was the next test the LORD instructed Gideon to perform after reducing the number to ten thousand?
options: Bring them down to the water to try them
Send spies to the Midianite camp
Divide them into three companies
Take away all their weapons
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them down to the water to try them
questions.explanation: Judges 7:4 instructs Gideon to bring the people down to the water to try them further.

questions.question: According to the LORD's command, which men were to be set apart at the water?
options: Those who lapped the water with their tongue like a dog
Those who bowed down on their knees to drink
Those who drank water from their hands
Those who refused to drink water
questions.correctAnswer: Those who lapped the water with their tongue like a dog
questions.explanation: Judges 7:5 states that those who lapped the water with their tongue like a dog were to be set apart.

questions.question: How many men lapped the water putting their hand to their mouth?
options: Three hundred
Ten thousand
Twenty-two thousand
One thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred
questions.explanation: Judges 7:6 says that three hundred men lapped the water with their hands to their mouths.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would do by the three hundred men who lapped the water?
options: Save Israel and deliver the Midianites into Gideon's hand
Bring more people to join the battle
Make the Midianites flee without fighting
Give the men great strength
questions.correctAnswer: Save Israel and deliver the Midianites into Gideon's hand
questions.explanation: Judges 7:7 indicates that by the three hundred men, the LORD would save them and deliver the Midianites.

questions.question: What did Gideon's men take with them after the number was reduced to three hundred?
options: Victuals and trumpets
Swords and shields
Bows and arrows
Spears and helmets
questions.correctAnswer: Victuals and trumpets
questions.explanation: Judges 7:8 states the men took victuals and trumpets.

questions.question: In what direction was the host of Midian located relative to Gideon's camp?
options: On the north side by the hill of Moreh
On the south side near the Jordan
East of mount Gilead
West of the well of Harod
questions.correctAnswer: On the north side by the hill of Moreh
questions.explanation: Judges 7:1 notes the host of Midian was on the north side by the hill of Moreh.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Gideon to keep all ten thousand men to fight the Midianites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 7:3-7 shows that Gideon was told to reduce the number first to ten thousand, then to three hundred men.

questions.question: True or False: Gideon went down to the Midianite camp with his servant Phurah because he was afraid.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 7:10-11 indicates that Gideon was told to go down with his servant Phurah if he feared going alone.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Gideon the very same night to get down to the Midianite host.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 7:9 states that the same night the LORD told Gideon to arise and go down to the host.

questions.question: True or False: The people who bowed on their knees to drink water were the ones chosen to fight alongside Gideon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 7:6 shows that those who lapped with their tongue were chosen, not those who bowed down to drink.

questions.question: Which comes first in Judges 7: the LORD telling Gideon to reduce the number of men by fearfulness or bringing them down to the water to try them?
options: Telling them to depart if fearful
Bringing them down to the water
Dividing the men into companies
Blowing the trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: Telling them to depart if fearful
questions.explanation: Judges 7:3 happens before Judges 7:4 where the people are first told to leave if fearful and then brought to the water.

questions.question: How did the LORD describe the Midianites and their camels in the valley?
options: Like grasshoppers for multitude, camels without number
Like lions in the field, camels few in number
Like trees in the forest, camels on the hills
Like waves of the sea, camels scattered
questions.correctAnswer: Like grasshoppers for multitude, camels without number
questions.explanation: Judges 7:12 describes the Midianites as lying like grasshoppers for multitude and camels as numerous as sand by the sea.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Judges 7:10-11, why did God instruct Gideon to go down to the Midianite host with his servant Phurah?
options: To hear what the enemy was saying and gain courage to fight
To spy out the land for a better battle position
To negotiate peace with the Midianites
To gather more troops for the battle
questions.correctAnswer: To hear what the enemy was saying and gain courage to fight
questions.explanation: Judges 7:10 says God told Gideon to go down with Phurah if he feared going alone, and Judges 7:11 explains that hearing what the enemy said would strengthen his hands to go down to the host.

questions.question: How does Judges 7:12 describe the size and number of the Midianite host and their camels?
options: They were as numerous as grasshoppers and their camels as the sand by the sea
They were few in number but had many horses
They were numerous but had few camels
They were like a small flock of sheep
questions.correctAnswer: They were as numerous as grasshoppers and their camels as the sand by the sea
questions.explanation: Judges 7:12 states the Midianites and their allies lay along in the valley like grasshoppers for multitude, and their camels were without number, like the sand by the sea.

questions.question: What was the content and significance of the dream told in Judges 7:13-14?
options: A cake of barley bread tumbled into the Midianite camp and caused a tent to fall, interpreted as God delivering Midian into Gideon's hand
A lion roaring over the camp, symbolizing Gideon's strength
A river overflowing and washing away the enemy, representing God's power
A sun rising and shining on Israel, meaning victory was near
questions.correctAnswer: A cake of barley bread tumbled into the Midianite camp and caused a tent to fall, interpreted as God delivering Midian into Gideon's hand
questions.explanation: Verses 7:13-14 describe a man dreaming of barley bread tumbling into the Midianite camp and overturning a tent, which his fellow interprets as the sword of Gideon, God’s instrument to deliver Midian.

questions.question: Based on Judges 7:15, how did Gideon respond after hearing the dream and its interpretation?
options: He worshipped and encouraged the Israelite host to arise because the Lord delivered Midian
He doubted and asked for more signs
He feared and retreated to his tent
He sent spies to confirm the dream
questions.correctAnswer: He worshipped and encouraged the Israelite host to arise because the Lord delivered Midian
questions.explanation: Judges 7:15 shows Gideon worshipped upon hearing the dream’s interpretation and told the people to arise because the Lord had delivered Midian into their hands.

questions.question: What tactical approach did Gideon take with his 300 men according to Judges 7:16-17?
options: Dividing them into three companies, each with trumpets, empty pitchers, and lamps, and instructing them to imitate his actions
Positioning them all together for a direct charge
Sending half to attack and half to defend the camp
Hiding them in the valley to ambush the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing them into three companies, each with trumpets, empty pitchers, and lamps, and instructing them to imitate his actions
questions.explanation: Verses 7:16-17 explain Gideon divided his men into three companies, gave each a trumpet, pitcher, and lamp, and told them to do as he did at the camp’s edge.

questions.question: What was the signal for the men to blow their trumpets as described in Judges 7:18?
options: When Gideon blew the trumpet, all were to blow theirs simultaneously and shout 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon'
When the sun rose, they were to blow the trumpets
Upon seeing the enemy sleep, they were to blow the trumpets
At the sound of a bell from the camp
questions.correctAnswer: When Gideon blew the trumpet, all were to blow theirs simultaneously and shout 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon'
questions.explanation: Judges 7:18 states that Gideon would blow the trumpet first, then all would blow their trumpets on every side of the camp and cry out the specified phrase.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 7:19-20, Gideon's men broke their pitchers and held lamps in their right hands during the attack.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 7:20 states they held lamps in their left hands and trumpets in their right hands, then blew the trumpets and broke the pitchers.

questions.question: What was the immediate effect of Gideon’s attack on the Midianite camp as described in Judges 7:21?
options: The Midianites ran, cried, and fled
They fought fiercely and repelled Gideon’s men
They surrendered immediately
They called for reinforcements
questions.correctAnswer: The Midianites ran, cried, and fled
questions.explanation: Judges 7:21 clearly states that the host ran, cried, and fled after Gideon's men stood in their places surrounding the camp.

questions.question: How does Judges 7:22 show God's intervention during the battle?
options: God set every man's sword against his fellow causing confusion and flight
God sent an earthquake to scare the enemy
God caused a storm to block the enemy’s path
God provided extra weapons to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God set every man's sword against his fellow causing confusion and flight
questions.explanation: Judges 7:22 explains that the Lord caused the Midianites to fight among themselves, turning their swords against each other, which led to their flight.

questions.question: According to Judges 7:23-24, what role did the men of Israel from Naphtali, Asher, Manasseh, and Ephraim play after the initial victory?
options: They gathered and pursued the fleeing Midianites, securing the waters at Bethbarah and Jordan
They rested and celebrated at the camp
They built defensive fortifications
They negotiated a treaty with Midian
questions.correctAnswer: They gathered and pursued the fleeing Midianites, securing the waters at Bethbarah and Jordan
questions.explanation: Verses 7:23-24 describe how the men of Israel assembled from various tribes to pursue Midian and secured the waters at Bethbarah and Jordan to prevent Midian’s escape.

questions.question: What biblical virtue can be learned from Gideon’s obedience in dividing his men and following God’s unusual battle plan in Judges 7:16-18?
options: Faith and trust in God’s guidance even when it seems unconventional
Pride in one's own military strategy
Self-reliance over divine instruction
Avoidance of risk at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and trust in God’s guidance even when it seems unconventional
questions.explanation: Judges 7:16-18 show Gideon obeying God’s command to use trumpets, pitchers, and lamps in a strange tactic, teaching believers to trust God’s guidance despite unusual methods.

questions.question: What does Judges 7:15-16 teach about responding to God’s promises in challenging situations?
options: Worship and take decisive action in faith when God reveals His plan
Wait passively for God to act without personal involvement
Ignore divine messages and rely on human plans
Delay action until all fears are removed
questions.correctAnswer: Worship and take decisive action in faith when God reveals His plan
questions.explanation: Judges 7:15-16 show Gideon worshipping after hearing God’s promise and immediately organizing his men for battle, exemplifying faith and prompt obedience.

questions.question: According to Judges 7:13-15, what role does hearing and interpreting God’s message play in strengthening faith?
options: It encourages worship and bold action by revealing God’s control over circumstances
It causes confusion and fear about the future
It leads to doubt and indecision
It requires secret rituals before acting
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages worship and bold action by revealing God’s control over circumstances
questions.explanation: The dream and its interpretation in Judges 7:13-15 reveal God’s control, causing Gideon to worship and confidently lead his men.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 7:18 teaches that proclaiming 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon' during the attack was a way to declare God’s power and encourage Israel’s faith.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 7:18 commands the men to blow trumpets and cry out 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon,' signifying reliance on God’s power and bolstering morale.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 7:25 records that Gideon personally killed the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 7:25 states that the men of Israel took and slew Oreb and Zeeb and brought their heads to Gideon, not that Gideon personally killed them.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 7.

questions.question: What was Gideon's strategy before attacking the Midianite camp as described in Judges 7:19-20?
options: Blowing trumpets, breaking pitchers, and holding lamps
Charging directly with swords drawn
Setting fire to the camp
Sending messengers to negotiate
questions.correctAnswer: Blowing trumpets, breaking pitchers, and holding lamps
questions.explanation: Judges 7:19-20 describe Gideon and his men blowing trumpets and breaking pitchers that contained lamps, using the lamps and trumpets as a psychological warfare tactic to confuse and frighten the enemy.

questions.question: What was the immediate effect on the Midianite camp when Gideon and his men executed their attack plan?
options: The host ran, cried, and fled
They fought bravely and repelled the attack
They captured Gideon and his men
They surrendered peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: The host ran, cried, and fled
questions.explanation: Judges 7:21 states that after Gideon's attack, the Midianite host was thrown into panic, causing them to run, cry out, and flee from the camp.

questions.question: What unique act did the LORD perform during the battle to aid Gideon's victory?
options: Set every man's sword against his fellow
Sent a thunderstorm to disrupt the enemy
Caused an earthquake to scatter the enemy
Made the enemy blind
questions.correctAnswer: Set every man's sword against his fellow
questions.explanation: Judges 7:22 describes that the LORD caused confusion by setting every Midianite's sword against his fellow, leading to their self-destruction and flight.

questions.question: From which tribes of Israel did the men gather to pursue the fleeing Midianites after the battle?
options: Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh
Judah, Simeon, and Levi
Reuben, Gad, and Ephraim
Benjamin, Dan, and Zebulun
questions.correctAnswer: Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh
questions.explanation: Judges 7:23 mentions that men from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh came together to pursue the Midianite forces after their defeat.

questions.question: What instruction did Gideon send to the men of Mount Ephraim during the pursuit of the Midianites?
options: Come down against the Midianites and take before them the waters unto Bethbarah and Jordan
Wait in the mountains for reinforcements
Build fortifications along the Jordan River
Offer peace terms to the Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: Come down against the Midianites and take before them the waters unto Bethbarah and Jordan
questions.explanation: Judges 7:24 records that Gideon sent messengers to Mount Ephraim urging them to block the Midianites' retreat by taking control of the waters at Bethbarah and Jordan.

questions.question: Who were the two princes of the Midianites captured and killed according to Judges 7:25?
options: Oreb and Zeeb
Sihon and Og
Abimelech and Jotham
Eglon and Ehud
questions.correctAnswer: Oreb and Zeeb
questions.explanation: Judges 7:25 states that the two Midianite princes taken and killed were Oreb and Zeeb, whose deaths symbolized the defeat of Midian.

questions.question: What literary device best describes the use of the dream about the barley cake in Judges 7:13-14?
options: Foreshadowing of Gideon's victory
Parable about faith
Allegory of Israel's restoration
Hyperbole about Midianite strength
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing of Gideon's victory
questions.explanation: Judges 7:13-14 uses a dream narrative as a foreshadowing device, symbolizing the destruction of Midian by Gideon's hand, preparing the reader for the coming victory.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon' function literarily in Judges 7:20?
options: As an inclusio linking divine authority with human agency
As a metaphor for peace and reconciliation
As a direct quote from a Midianite chant
As a lamentation for the fallen
questions.correctAnswer: As an inclusio linking divine authority with human agency
questions.explanation: Judges 7:20 uses the phrase to emphasize that the victory is both God's work and Gideon's, serving as an inclusio that frames the narrative with divine-human cooperation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 300 men who lapped water by hand in Judges 7:6 in the Hebrew word study of 'lap' (שָׁקַק, shaqaq)?
options: It implies alertness and readiness rather than careless drinking
It means they drank excessively and were weak
It signifies ritual purification before battle
It denotes a careless or unworthy action
questions.correctAnswer: It implies alertness and readiness rather than careless drinking
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root שָׁקַק (shaqaq) suggests lapping water quickly and alertly, distinguishing these men as watchful soldiers, as described in Judges 7:6.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God using few to defeat many as seen in Judges 7?
options: 1 Corinthians 1:27
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:32
James 2:14
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 1:27
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:27 highlights God choosing the weak and few to shame the strong and many, paralleling the theme in Judges 7 where God uses 300 men to defeat a vast army.

questions.question: True or False: Gideon's command to his men to blow trumpets and break pitchers was an example of psychological warfare designed to create confusion among the enemy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: As Judges 7:19-20 shows, Gideon's tactics caused panic and confusion, making the enemy think they were surrounded by a large force, demonstrating psychological warfare.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar motif of God delivering enemies into the hands of a seemingly weaker chosen leader as Judges 7 portrays Gideon?
options: 1 Samuel 17 (David and Goliath)
Exodus 14 (Crossing the Red Sea)
Joshua 6 (Fall of Jericho)
Daniel 3 (Fiery Furnace)
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 17 (David and Goliath)
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17 recounts God enabling young David to defeat the giant Goliath, a story that, like Judges 7, underscores God's power to save through unlikely means.

questions.question: What cultural significance did the use of trumpets and lamps in ancient Near Eastern warfare have, as reflected in Gideon's battle plan?
options: They served as signals for coordination and surprise attacks
They were used primarily for religious ceremonies, not battle
They indicated surrender or parley
They were a form of entertainment during war
questions.correctAnswer: They served as signals for coordination and surprise attacks
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern warfare, trumpets were used to signal troops, and lamps could create illusions of greater numbers, both of which Gideon employed for surprise and confusion (Judges 7:16-20).

questions.question: True or False: After the initial victory, Gideon immediately became king over Israel as a result of the battle in Judges 7.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 7 does not record Gideon becoming king; rather, he remains a judge and military leader, in keeping with the period's decentralized leadership (noted throughout Judges).

questions.question: What does the dream about the barley cake tumbling into the Midianite camp symbolize in relation to agricultural imagery and Israel's deliverance?
options: The destruction of Midian by a humble but effective force
The abundance of Israel's crops after victory
The futility of Midian's agricultural efforts
A warning about famine in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The destruction of Midian by a humble but effective force
questions.explanation: The barley cake, a simple staple, falling and destroying the tent symbolizes how God will use a small, seemingly insignificant force (Gideon and 300 men) to overthrow the powerful Midianites (Judges 7:13-14).

theological.title: Judges Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological principle is demonstrated by the Lord's instruction to reduce Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300 men?
options: God desires Israel to trust in His power, not their numbers
God wants to punish Israel for their fearfulness
God values only the strongest warriors
God intends to confuse the Midianites with a small force
questions.correctAnswer: God desires Israel to trust in His power, not their numbers
questions.explanation: Judges 7:2-7 shows that God deliberately reduced the army so that Israel would not boast that their own hand saved them, highlighting dependence on divine power rather than human strength.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily revealed when God instructs Gideon to test the men by how they drink water?
options: Omniscience
Omnipotence
Sovereignty
Immanence
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Judges 7:4-6 illustrates God's sovereign authority in selecting the 300 men by a unique test, demonstrating His control over the outcome and means of salvation.

questions.question: What does the dream of the barley cake tumbling into the Midianite camp symbolize in relation to God's redemptive narrative?
options: The coming of a humble deliverer who will overthrow enemies
The destruction of Israel's enemies by natural disasters
The abundance of food in Israel’s future
The alliance between Israel and Midian
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of a humble deliverer who will overthrow enemies
questions.explanation: Judges 7:13-14 symbolizes God's use of an unlikely instrument—Gideon, a humble man like barley bread—to deliver Israel, foreshadowing the biblical theme of God raising humble saviors.

questions.question: How does Gideon's worship after hearing the dream and its interpretation reveal a key aspect of sanctification?
options: Recognition of God's sovereignty leads to worship and obedience
Worship is only for grand miracles, not dreams
Sanctification is solely about ritual purity
God’s judgment is feared but not worshipped
questions.correctAnswer: Recognition of God's sovereignty leads to worship and obedience
questions.explanation: Judges 7:15 shows Gideon worshipping and then encouraging action, indicating sanctification involves responding in worship and obedience to God's revealed will.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the Lord setting every man's sword against his fellow in the Midianite camp?
options: Divine judgment executed through human instruments
Human free will determines victory
Salvation by works
The inevitability of human conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment executed through human instruments
questions.explanation: Judges 7:22 reveals that God orchestrates the Midianite defeat by causing confusion and internal strife, demonstrating that divine judgment can operate through human agency.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's testing and human response is conveyed by Judges 7:3-4 and Judges 7:11?
options: God tests faith to strengthen and prepare His people for victory
God tests people arbitrarily without purpose
Human fear disqualifies from God's service
Testing is only for leaders, not the people
questions.correctAnswer: God tests faith to strengthen and prepare His people for victory
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 show God testing the people by fear and water drinking, while verse 11 encourages Gideon to listen and gain strength, illustrating that divine testing is purposeful for growth and readiness.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Gideon dividing his men with trumpets, pitchers, and lamps reflect a typological foreshadowing of Christ's victory?
options: It symbolizes spiritual warfare where light overcomes darkness
It represents military strategy without spiritual meaning
It shows reliance on human weapons only
It prefigures the destruction of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes spiritual warfare where light overcomes darkness
questions.explanation: Judges 7:16-20 typologically points to Christ as the true light overcoming darkness, with lamps inside pitchers symbolizing hidden strength and trumpet blasts as proclamation of divine victory.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized when He reassures Gideon to go down to the Midianite camp because He has delivered it into his hand?
options: Faithfulness
Wrath
Jealousy
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Judges 7:9 shows God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His promise to Gideon by delivering the enemy into his hands, encouraging trust in divine promises.

questions.question: In the broader redemptive story of Scripture, how does Judges 7:25's account of the execution of Oreb and Zeeb contribute?
options: It demonstrates God’s judgment upon enemy princes as part of Israel’s deliverance
It indicates the end of all warfare in Israel
It shows Israel’s failure to trust God
It is unrelated to the theme of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s judgment upon enemy princes as part of Israel’s deliverance
questions.explanation: The killing of Oreb and Zeeb in Judges 7:25 typifies God’s triumph over enemies through His chosen deliverer, contributing to the narrative of God’s redemptive justice.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about human fear and divine empowerment is revealed by the reduction of Gideon's army when fearful men leave, and later when Gideon is encouraged to hear the enemy's talk?
options: God removes fearful to refine faith and strengthens leaders through assurance
Fear is a sign of sin that disqualifies completely
God punishes those who fear by removing them
Human strength alone ensures victory
questions.correctAnswer: God removes fearful to refine faith and strengthens leaders through assurance
questions.explanation: Judges 7:3 and 7:10-11 show God allowing fearful men to leave and giving Gideon encouragement, teaching that God refines faith by removing doubt and strengthening the faithful.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the miraculous victory in Judges 7 is merely a psychological trick with no divine involvement. What does Judges 7:19-22 actually teach about God's role in the battle?
options: God actively intervenes by causing confusion and turning enemies against each other
Victory was due solely to human surprise tactics
The Midianites fled because of natural disasters
The text suggests the event was a myth with no real battle
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes by causing confusion and turning enemies against each other
questions.explanation: Verses 19-22 describe God's supernatural act of setting each man's sword against his fellow, clearly indicating divine intervention beyond human strategy.

questions.question: What does the instruction to blow trumpets and shout 'The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon' reveal about the nature of God’s deliverance?
options: God’s deliverance is both divine and mediated through His chosen servant
Victory depends only on human power
God’s name is not important in battle
Deliverance is random and unplanned
questions.correctAnswer: God’s deliverance is both divine and mediated through His chosen servant
questions.explanation: Judges 7:18-20 shows that victory is attributed both to the LORD and Gideon, emphasizing God’s deliverance through human instruments.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about human leadership and divine empowerment can be drawn from Judges 7:1 and Judges 7:23-24?
options: God raises leaders like Gideon who, empowered by Him, unite Israel for deliverance
Leadership is irrelevant to God’s plan
Israel’s tribes act independently without divine guidance
Human leaders are sufficient without God
questions.correctAnswer: God raises leaders like Gideon who, empowered by Him, unite Israel for deliverance
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 23-24 show Gideon rallying Israel and Ephraim’s men joining, highlighting God’s raising of leaders who unify His people for salvation.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by His use of a small, seemingly insignificant group of 300 men to defeat a vast army?
options: Omnipotence
Immutability
Holiness
Eternity
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Judges 7:7 demonstrates God’s omnipotence in achieving victory through a drastically reduced force, showing His all-powerful ability to save.

questions.question: What does the practice of breaking pitchers and holding lamps inside during the night attack symbolize about spiritual warfare and sanctification?
options: Breaking old ways to reveal the light of faith in action
A purely tactical military maneuver
An act of despair
A ritual for good luck
questions.correctAnswer: Breaking old ways to reveal the light of faith in action
questions.explanation: Judges 7:20’s breaking of pitchers to reveal lamps symbolizes the destruction of old reliance and the illumination of God’s power, a metaphor for sanctification in spiritual battle.
